name: ethanol
source: Heywood, John B., Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, McGraw-Hill, 1988, Table 9.7 'Oxygenate properties', p. 477, 'Ethanol' column: lower heating value 26.8 MJ/kg, specific gravity 0.794 (Table 9.7 states no reference temperature); density taken as 0.794 x 1000 kg/m^3 = 794.0 kg/m^3 (derived). Against water at 15 degC (999.1 kg/m^3) it would be 793.3 kg/m^3, -0.1 %, below the table's own 3-digit precision. Stoichiometric air/fuel mass ratio 9.0: Heywood 1988 Table 9.7, 'Stoichiometric (A/F)' row, Ethanol column; the same book states (A/F)s = 9.00 in the text following Eq. (3.11), p. 72 (the stoichiometric equation C2H5OH + 3(O2 + 3.773 N2) = 2CO2 + 3H2O + 11.32N2). Cross-check (derived): 3 mol O2 x 4.773 mol air/mol O2 x 28.96 g/mol / 46.07 g/mol = 9.001. This is anhydrous fuel-grade ethanol (EN 15376 blending component), not hydrous ethanol - the value used as the '100%' endpoint (v = 1) of the physics_sim.fuel/1 ethanol blend mixing rule (see data/fuels/e5.json/e10.json/e25.json/e85.json and docs/data_formats/fuel.md).
